newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain Repsol gains as share offer kicks off.
newsitem.headline: Spain Repsol gains as share offer kicks off.

text.p: Shares in Repsol were higher in early trade on Monday, buoyed by strong demand as the sale of the Spanish government's last 10 percent stake in the energy group kicked off, dealers said.
At 1030 GMT, Repsol was up 70 pesetas, or 1.2 percent, to 5,910 pesetas. The Ibex-35 index of leading shares was up 1.78 percent to 5,431.24.
"Repsol is recovering from a recent low of around 5,800 pesetas, but in the last week it has still outperformed both Telefonica and Endesa," said one dealer at a Spanish bank.
The shares are expected to stay in positive territory today, but far below a previous record high of 6,100 pesetas.
The fact that the number of shares on sale is relatively small and that the privatisation is widely expected to be successful is supporting the stock, dealers added.

The period for provisional share orders opens today and runs to April 21, with the 12.75 million shares on offer to the Spanish public widely expected to be snapped up. The sale price --to be set on April 28-- will offer a four percent discount for small shareholders.
Analysts expect the sale price to be set at around 6,000 pesetas.
